THE BEGINNING OF A LONGER JOURNEY", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u053-b0121", "target": "— Долго, видать, пройдёт, — тихо сказал мистер Пегготи, — пока у лодки найдутся новые жильцы. Здесь, внизу, её теперь считают несчастливой!", "source_sha256": "4601183ea2aac014b75c9270e87dd9621d27e0300d82d9a18a396531d1d5f8f6", "target_id": "ru-en85-u053-b0121", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "c41df1b0a22edaab6d668f7c630361db7a5ea3f08a94dcc7434736c41f3e369f"}, {"source_id": "en85-u053-b0122", "target": "— Она принадлежит кому-нибудь из здешних? — спросил я.", "source_sha256": "2e6a71474729784c73b18de8745883dcea90a2a7853ece02fa034075ac1151ce", "target_id": "ru-en85-u053-b0122", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "92cac7e36b6c300cd35f1654cd0374c3149a56c739f17728240803695718dcf1"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 51, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u053-b0123", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To a mast-maker up town,’ said Mr. Peggotty. ‘I’m a-going to give the key to him tonight.’", "sha256": "598adcaae7a9676038379b4c5ee453ade8ffb24aa57579393731326208f6ee3e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[124]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0124", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We looked into the other little room, and came back to Mrs. Gummidge, sitting on the locker, whom Mr. Peggotty, putting the light on the chimney-piece, requested to rise, that he might carry it outside the door before extinguishing the candle.", "sha256": "d2a8c97dddeced6543ef3b8840bd15adddf49221c3ad35b317f810a81f35e5ea", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[125]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0125", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Dan’l,’ said Mrs. Gummidge, suddenly deserting her basket, and clinging to his arm ‘my dear Dan’l, the parting words I speak in this house is, I mustn’t be left behind. Doen’t ye think of leaving me behind, Dan’l! Oh, doen’t ye ever do it!’", "sha256": "6921af6bc071b5a9c2ad2f7dd548d14c05e872cd41a81fbe4341baa59080dcf0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[126]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0126", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Peggotty, taken aback, looked from Mrs. Gummidge to me, and from me to Mrs. Gummidge, as if he had been awakened from a sleep.", "sha256": "37b14d5a59764cd499e40b85deb77e9ad7778fc220952cd7f1d7ae22b9cd0640", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[127]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0127", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Doen’t ye, dearest Dan’l, doen’t ye!’ cried Mrs. Gummidge, fervently. ‘Take me ‘long with you, Dan’l, take me ‘long with you and Em’ly! I’ll be your servant, constant and trew. If there’s slaves in them parts where you’re a-going, I’ll be bound to you for one, and happy, but doen’t ye leave me behind, Dan’l, that’s a deary dear!’", "sha256": "cc06f430f42eb80b21728bf31e1be1548a2c718243ca3fa3378d02128f61672a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[128]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0128", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My good soul,’ said Mr. Peggotty, shaking his head, ‘you doen’t know what a long voyage, and what a hard life ‘tis!’ ‘Yes, I do, Dan’l! I can guess!’ cried Mrs. Gummidge. ‘But my parting words under this roof is, I shall go into the house and die, if I am not took. I can dig, Dan’l. I can work. I can live hard. I can be loving and patient now—more than you think, Dan’l, if you’ll on’y try me. I wouldn’t touch the ‘lowance, not if I was dying of want, Dan’l Peggotty; but I’ll go with you and Em’ly, if you’ll on’y let me, to the world’s end! I know how ‘tis; I know you think that I am lone and lorn; but, deary love, ‘tan’t so no more! I ain’t sat here, so long, a-watching, and a-thinking of your trials, without some good being done me. Mas’r Davy, speak to him for me! I knows his ways, and Em’ly’s, and I knows their sorrows, and can be a comfort to ‘em, some odd times, and labour for ‘em allus! Dan’l, deary Dan’l, let me go ‘long with you!’", "sha256": "45f4ff27d480f0a40f9827fb2e73f28c65b00d6632f7607b8ef278c480b78b74", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[129]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0129", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "And Mrs. Gummidge took his hand, and kissed it with a homely pathos and affection, in a homely rapture of devotion and gratitude, that he well deserved.", "sha256": "e5aa5945e56060a7220837f94030dc1999bc7aad8d1164c938c3081dce9e9a44", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[130]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u053-b0130", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We brought the locker out, extinguished the candle, fastened the door on the outside, and left the old boat close shut up, a dark speck in the cloudy night. Next day, when we were returning to London outside the coach, Mrs. Gummidge and her basket were on the seat behind, and Mrs. Gummidge was happy.", "sha256": "5df1e852a8c36560febcf1610eda1a926e51b9e5df2e3b6c2897f45fa011cd7d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[58]/p[131]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
